# Boule Governance Framework: Tariff and Legal Adaptation Procedures

## (a) Tariff Procedure

The boule shall convene a Tariff Committee of no fewer than five members when commercial conditions require schedule adjustment. The Committee must publish a draft schedule publicly for no fewer than ten days before the boule votes, allowing merchants to submit objections. Emergency tariff adjustments—defined as responses to sudden trade disruptions, embargoes, or rapid currency fluctuation—may be enacted provisionally by a two-thirds boule vote and reported to the Archon within seventy-two hours; these expire after sixty days unless ratified through standard procedure. All adopted tariff schedules take effect on the first day of the next market month and are logged in the Civic Archive, open to central government inspection.

## (b) Decision Matrix with Approval Paths

| Category | Description | Approval Path |
|---|---|---|
| **1. Routine tariffs** | Adjustments within 15% of existing rates, affecting fewer than twenty commodity lines | Boule vote only; reported to Archon within five days |
| **2. Significant tariff reform** | Changes exceeding 15%, new categories, or broader economic impact | Boule proposes; Archon ratifies within thirty days; if Archon withholds, EkKlesia may override by simple majority |
| **3. Legal code adaptation** | Amendments to commercial dispute procedure, contract enforcement, or merchant custom recognition | Boule proposes; EkKlesia deliberates and votes; Archon certifies consistency with central code; central government may nullify within ninety days |
| **4. Diplomatic trade arrangements** | Formal tariff agreements, mutual recognition, or preferential treatment with foreign powers | Boule advises; Archon negotiates; central government approves; EkKlesia informed |

Matters touching criminal law, property rights outside commerce, or constitutional structure require central government authorization regardless of boule recommendation.

## (c) Legal Adaptation Mechanism

The boule may propose adaptations to commercial law only within the following constraints: adaptations must cite existing merchant custom or established precedent, may not contradict central legal code, and must include a compatibility certification from the Archon before enactment. All adaptations expire after five years unless renewed through the same procedure, preventing cumulative drift. The Dikasterion (auditing body) shall conduct a annual review of legal adaptations to detect jurisdictional creep toward either rival power, and may refer concerns to the EkKlesia for remedial action.

## (d) Composition and Rotation

The boule shall comprise twelve members elected by registered merchants meeting a minimum commercial threshold (annual transaction volume). No member may serve more than two consecutive one-year terms; after a one-year hiatus, prior service does not bar re-election. Officers rotate annually: the Prostates (presiding officer) may not serve more than one term. Membership is staggered so no more than half the boule turns over in a single election. The Archon may suspend any boule member pending investigation for corruption or foreign entanglement, subject to EkKlesia review within thirty days. These rules prevent permanent capture while drawing experienced merchants into governance.

# Garrison and Security Architecture for the Border Trade City

## (a) Chain of Command

The strategos is appointed by the central government, not by the city. Appointment requires confirmation by the Boule and Archon of the city, but their refusal triggers a mandatory 60-day consultation period after which central appointment stands unless both houses formally declare a conflict of interest and the central government concurs.

The strategos reports to the **Archon of the Border Provinces** (central ministry) and to the **Strategos of the Theater** (military theater commander). Dual reporting ensures no single chain can be captured. The strategos communicates through two independent courier routes; routine reports go through the provincial Archon, while intelligence and contingency operations are sent directly to the theater commander with copies sealed to the provincial Archon.

To prevent capture by the merchant elite: the strategos is prohibited from holding property in the city or its hinterland, from marrying a resident, and from conducting private trade. Financial disclosure is required quarterly to the Dikasterion (central auditing body). To prevent foreign co-option: the strategos rotates every 24 months; a replacement is named before the outgoing departs, and during the transition both are present simultaneously — the predecessor holds no command authority but remains as observer for 30 days.

## (b) Asset Allocation

**Central control (non-negotiable):**
- City walls and their gates — all key-laying and repair authority resides with the strategos
- Customs forts on the approaches — garrisoned by central troops, not city levies
- The intelligence bureau (see section d)
- Any artillery, siege trains, or heavy arms

**Locally managed:**
- Local watch (city police) — maintains order in markets and residential quarters; reports to the Archon
- Market police — enforces commercial codes under the Boule's authority
- Neighborhood defense corps — voluntary, armed with sidearms only, for fire and flood response

The city may arm its local watch with spears and short swords but not crossbows, cavalry, or any weapon with range exceeding 50 meters. The strategos conducts an annual inventory of all weapons held within the city walls.

## (c) Override Triggers and Procedure

The strategos may override the Boule or Archon only on explicit security grounds: confirmed foreign intelligence operation, imminent external threat, or credible evidence of a coup attempt. The trigger must be documented in a written *proclamation of necessity* filed simultaneously with the provincial Archon and the theater commander, and publicly posted in the agora within six hours.

During override, the strategos may:
- Seal the gates (suspend trade) for a maximum of 72 hours without further authorization
- Detain individuals named in the proclamation for questioning, up to 48 hours
- Requisition goods and transport for defense purposes with compensation set by the Archon within 30 days

The strategos may NOT use override to:
- Collect taxes or tariffs
- Arrest individuals for speech or commerce offenses
- Install or remove city officials
- Modify commercial agreements

The Boule may petition the Dikasterion to vacate an override at any time; the Dikasterion rules within 15 days. Any override exceeding 72 hours requires explicit written approval from the theater commander.

## (d) Counter-Intelligence Posture

The intelligence bureau operates under the strategos but is staffed separately from garrison duties. Its mandate covers: foreign diplomatic personnel and their local contacts, merchant houses with ties to rival powers, and any organization receiving funding from outside the city.

The bureau maintains a **merchant接触 register** — any contact between a foreign diplomatic agent and a city merchant beyond routine customs brokerage must be reported within 24 hours by the merchant. Failure to report is a commercial code violation, not a security crime; penalties are fines and temporary trade suspension, not imprisonment.

To avoid paralyzing trade: the bureau operates on a **red/yellow/green** threat tier refreshed monthly. Green status imposes no operational restrictions beyond the contact register. Yellow status (elevated foreign activity not yet constituting a threat) requires the strategos to notify the Archon and Boule in closed session but imposes no public measures. Red status (confirmed hostile operation) triggers the override mechanism.

The bureau does not conduct surveillance of ordinary commerce, does not have undercover agents in market stalls, and may not intercept merchant correspondence except under a specific judicial warrant from the Dikasterion. Foreign merchants enjoy the same legal protections as citizens unless individually named in a red-tier designation.

# Archon's Charter: Executive Oversight and Ratification Framework

## (a) Veto Scope

**The Archon may block the following categories of boule decision:**

1. **Treaties and compacts with foreign powers** — any agreement, memorandum, or informal understanding between the city and an external sovereign, regardless of whether it bears the name "treaty."
2. **Tariff schedules that diverge from the central schedule by more than the permitted flex band** — the archon retains a hard veto on protectionist or discriminatory rates that would constitute de facto diplomatic signaling to one neighboring power.
3. **Granting of extraterritorial legal privileges** to foreign merchants, envoys, or resident aliens, includingarbitration rights before foreign tribunals.
4. **Admission or expulsion of foreign consuls and the accreditation of rhetores** — the archon must countersign any credential before it takes effect.
5. **Decisions affecting the city garrison, fortress access, or the fortification of the walls** — military-related boule resolutions touching central defense fall within the archon's veto, as do resolutions to admit foreign troops or to demolish defensive works.
6. **Constitutional amendments and Organic Law revisions** — any boule resolution altering the city's autonomous charter or the succession of its magistrates.

**The archon has NO veto (or a merely declaratory, non-justiciable veto) over:**

1. **Internal tax assessment and land registration** — the boule's authority to value property, allocate liturgies, and assess local levies is not subject to archon veto; the archon may lodge a formal protest to the central government, but the veto does not suspend execution.
2. **Cultural and religious ordinances** — festivals, temple administration, and matters of local cult practice are outside the archon's veto unless they involve foreign religious personnel with political functions, in which case category (4) above applies.

---

## (b) Licensing of Foreign-Facing Officials

The rhetor and any magistrate who formally represents the city to foreign powers — including trade envoys, cultural ambassadors, and ad hoc diplomatic agents — must hold a **letter of credentials** issued jointly by the archon and ratified by the boule. The archon alone initiates the process by issuing a **nomination with conditions**; the boule votes to confirm or reject without power to substitute a different nominee.

**License contents** must include: the official's full name and domicile, the specific envoys and powers to which they may speak, the expiry date (no license exceeds twelve months), and any express limitations on commitments the rhetor may bind the city to.

**Revocation** is unilateral by the archon upon written finding of: (a) unauthorized commitment of the city, (b) acceptance of gifts or patronage from a foreign power, or (c) communication in secret channels outside the archon's knowledge. The archon files a **revocation return** with the central government within twenty-four hours; the boule receives a redacted copy. The central government may override a revocation within sixty days, but until it does, the revocation stands.

**Audit trail**: The archon maintains a **credential ledger** — a sealed, dual-keyed register deposited monthly with the central government and the city recorder. Each entry records issuance, conditions, use (periodic reports from the rhetor), and revocation. The central government audits annually; the boule may petition for a redacted extract.

---

## (c) Term and Rotation

**The archon serves a single non-renewable term of three years.** No individual may hold the archonship of this city more than once in any ten-year period, and no archon may immediately govern a second autonomous city upon departure.

**Selection**: The central government nominates three candidates from outside the city; the boule selects one. The archon-designate must satisfy a **no-conflict affidavit** — no property, marriage alliance, or litigation interest in the city or its neighboring powers for the preceding five years.

**Removal before term**: The central government may remove the archon for cause (treason, corruption, foreign capture) upon a two-thirds vote of the central council, with the boule afforded a formal hearing. The boule may also petition for removal by a two-thirds vote; the central government must respond within ninety days.

**Transition safeguards**: Upon departure, the archon may not hold city office, act as rhetor, or receive city contracts for two years. The archon's household members and close associates are barred from holding boule seats for one year post-departure — a deliberate break against local capture.

**Central tyranny prevention**: The archon's instructions are published to the boule at the start of each term. The archon may not amend the city's Organic Law, dissolve the boule, or suspend elections. The boule retains the right of **formal remonstrance** to the central government, and the archon may not retaliate against any boule member for such remonstrance.

---

## (d) Relationship to the Dikasterion

**The archon does not sit as judge or juror.** The dikasterion is the city's court of first and final instance for all civil and criminal matters within its jurisdiction, and its judges are drawn by lot from the citizen body in the traditional manner.

**The archon's prosecutorial function**: The archon may bring accusations before the dikasterion in two limited categories: (a) charges of treason against the city or central government, and (b) charges of foreign corruption — defined as acceptance of foreign payment, gift, or direction by any city official. These are the only charges the archon may initiate; for all other matters, prosecution rests with the thesmothetes and private litigants.

**Appointment andmagistracy**: The archon appoints no magistrates to the dikasterion. The dikasterion's presiding magistrates (the Eleven and the thesmothetes) are selected by lot and by the boule, as under the traditional constitution. The archon may not remove, suspend, or reassign any dikastic magistrate.

**Weaponization safeguards**: (1) The archon's right to prosecute is confined to the two categories above; any attempt to manufacture a foreign-corruption charge against a political opponent is itself a removable offense. (2) The dikasterion may not be prorogued, packed, or suspended by the archon under any emergency pretext. (3) Any citizen indicted by the archon may demand a transfer of the case to a neighboring city's dikasterion; the archon may not refuse the transfer. (4) The central government maintains a standing right to appoint an **advocate of the accused** to assist any defendant facing archon-brought charges, funded independently of the archon's budget.

## 边境城市自治框架：公民大会（Ekklesia）机制设计

### (a) 机制：公民参与的层次与边界

公民大会采用**三级参与权**结构，而非无限制的普遍投票权：

**第一级 — 专属决议权（Ekklesia自主决定）：**
地方市场管理、城区公共工程、本地商户纠纷仲裁、城市卫生与建筑规范。决议须经简单多数通过，议题由Boule提议或经50名公民联名提案。

**第二级 — 联合议决权（Ekklesia提议，中心批准）：**
关税税率调整（须在中心设定的上下限内）、本地法律编纂与修订、公共安全力量编制变更。Ekklesia以2/3多数提出建议，中心应在30日内批复；否决须附书面理由，Ekklesia可申诉。

**第三级 — 顾问征询权（Ekklesia提供意见，中心保留决定权）：**

# Rhetor Terms of Reference — Border Trade City Autonomy Negotiation

## (a) Credentials and Pre-Clearance Matrix

The Archon issues a **Segmented Credential Letter** upon appointment, partitioning authority into two spheres:

**Requires Pre-Clearance from the Archon (minimum 72-hour advance; emergency surcharge applies):**

1. Any commitment on **tariff rates or trade preferences** that outlast the current negotiating session
2. **Legal or judicial reciprocity agreements** — cross-border contract enforcement, extradition, or dispute resolution frameworks
3. **Diplomatic recognition or protocol** — titles, precedence, formal correspondence with foreign sovereigns
4. **Concessions affecting central revenue** —、盐税、關税split changes that touch the imperial exchequer
5. **Security or military arrangements** — garrison access, intelligence sharing, transit rights for armed parties

**Full Discretion On-Spot (no pre-clearance required):**

1. Procedural arrangements — meeting schedules, venue, interpreter services
2. Preliminary commercial offers and counter-offers in trade negotiations
3. Expressions of **goodwill and general mutual benefit** language (non-binding)
4. Requests for clarification on foreign party positions
5. **Hospitality and cultural exchange** logistics

---

## (b) Reporting and Audit

**Immediate Flash Report (within 4 hours of meeting conclusion):**
Transmitted via sealed courier to the Archon and the Boule secretary — a one-page summary: attendees, stated agenda, immediate outcomes, outstanding issues.

**Full Procès-Verbal (within 48 hours):**
A complete transcript or detailed minutes of every foreign meeting, filed with the Dikasterion clerk. This record is **publicly accessible** and immune from alteration once filed.

**Monthly Digest:**
The Rhetor compiles a 3-page summary of all foreign contacts, sentiment trends, and proposed commitments for the Boule's review session.

**On-Demand Audit:**
The Dikasterion may summon the Rhetor at any time for cross-examination. Failure to appear constitutes grounds for immediate credential revocation.

---

## (c) Political-Defense Posture

When a rival-power negotiator attempts to shift a commercial negotiation into political alignment — *e.g., "Your city clearly has interests distinct from the capital; let us discuss your independent future" —* the Rhetor is trained to deploy:

1. **The Fidelity Pivot:** *"My mandate is bounded by the terms the Archon has set; I speak only to commercial matters within that remit. If you have proposals on tariffs or trade terms, I am fully authorized to receive them."*

2. **The Mandate Boundary:** *"I note you speak of interests beyond my charge. I shall convey your words to the Archon. But I cannot receive proposals outside my credentials, nor commit the city to any position not pre-cleared."*

3. **The Counter-Offer Redirect:** *"You suggest our interests diverge — I hear you. But my purpose here is to expand trade, not to define political stances. Shall we return to the schedule of tariff reductions you proposed?"*

These moves are **scripted, rehearsed, and non-negotiable** — the Rhetor does not improvise political disclaimers.

---

## (d) Sunset and Revocation

**Void Ab Initio:** Any commitment made outside the credential letter — whether by accident, pressure, or ambition — is **void from the moment of utterance**. The foreign party bears the risk of relying on it.

**No Ratification Route:** The Rhetor may not retroactively validate an unauthorized commitment. The Archon alone may re-issue revised credentials, but this requires a fresh negotiation cycle, not a fix-up.

**Revocation Procedure:**
- The Archon issues a **revocation decree** publicly in the Agora
- A new Rhetor is appointed by the Boule within 72 hours
- The former Rhetor is subject to **Euthynai audit** within 30 days
- All foreign powers are notified via certified courier that prior credentials are terminated

**Note of Caution to the Rhetor:** Unauthorized commitments are treated not as administrative error but as **political transgression** — the penalty scale ranges from temporary debarment to permanent ostracism from diplomatic office, depending on severity and intent.

**DIKASTERION JUDGMENT — Judicial Review of the Border City Autonomy Framework**

---

**(a) Commercial Jurisdiction**

The framework assigns tariff and commercial law to the boule, but is silent on who resolves disputes arising under that law. This lacuna is unsafe.

*Prescription:* The boule's commercial court (symbouleutikon dikasterion) must have first-instance jurisdiction over disputes between two private parties where both are resident in the city, or where the contract was performed within city territory. Jurisdiction over disputes involving a foreign merchant (exterior mercator) must require at least one neutral arbitrator drawn from a shared-trade roster, or be referred directly to the central court's commercial chamber — not to the boule's own tribunal, which is structurally biased. 

*Appeal path:* Two-tier only. First appeal lies to the central government's commercial bureau (the analogue of the dikasterion's appellate jurisdiction) within 30 days of judgment. No third appeal on fact; only on manifest error of law or denial of due process may the matter reach the full central tribunal. This prevents the capital from being flooded while preserving a check on local capture.

*Foreign merchant protection:* The boule may not apply adapted law in a manner that discriminates against non-resident merchants on grounds of nationality. This non-discrimination principle must be expressly codified, not merely implied by "equal before the law." A foreign merchant who feels aggrieved by the first-instance commercial tribunal may bypass the 30-day wait and apply directly to the central court for an interlocutory injunction — this emergency access must be guaranteed by statute, not left to judicial discretion.

---

**(b) Veto Reviewability**

The archon holds veto on "sovereignty matters." Whether that veto is justiciable determines whether the archon is truly accountable or above the law.

*Prescription:* The archon's veto is reviewable on three grounds: (1) ultra vires — the matter the archon claimed was a sovereignty matter was in fact a commercial or civic administration matter within the boule's plenary competence; (2) procedural — the archon did not issue a written, reasoned decision within the statutory 15-day period following the boule's resolution; (3) manifest error — the archon's stated grounds are so implausible as to constitute a pretext. 

*Standing and forum:* The boule (as a collegiate body, not individual members) has standing to petition the central dikasterion for judicial review of a veto within 45 days. Individual citizens have standing only if the veto directly impairs a personal right, not merely a collective policy preference. The central dikasterion may affirm the veto, reverse it (in which case the boule's original resolution takes effect), or remand with instructions. The archon may not issue a second veto on the same resolution after a judicial reversal — that would constitute contempt.

---

**(c) Override Due Process**

The strategos's security override is the most dangerous power in the framework: it is exercisable in exigent circumstances, by definition without prior notice, and affects liberty and property. Without procedural rails, it becomes a tool for arbitrary rule.

*Prescription:* The following minimum due process protections must be embedded in the charter:

1. *Immediate written record:* Within 48 hours of exercising override, the strategos must file a sworn declaration with the city registrar and the central dikasterion specifying the factual basis for the override, the individuals affected, and the duration. Failure to file renders the override void ab initio.

2. *Post-hoc judicial review:* Any affected person or merchant may apply to the central dikasterion within 20 days for an order vacating the override or any resulting seizure/restraint. The strategos bears the burden of showing the override was necessary and proportionate — not the claimant.

3. *Compensation:* Property seized under override must be inventoried by a neutral magistrate and held in trust. Unjustified seizure (after final judicial determination) obligates the strategos's office, not the city treasury, to compensate at fair market value.

4. *Duration limit:* No override may persist beyond 60 days without renewal by the central government. Renewal requires fresh justification reviewed by the strategos's superior command.

5. *No expulsion without trial:* A citizen may not be expelled from the city under override — only detained pending review, and detention beyond 72 hours requires a judicial warrant from a neutral magistrate (which may be sought ex parte).

---

**(d) Status of Over-Committed Diplomatic Acts**

The rhetor's diplomatic credentials are bounded. The critical question is: what is the legal effect of a commitment the rhetor made that exceeds those bounds?

*Prescription:* Three categories must be distinguished:

# Integrated Governance Framework: Border Trade City

## Charter of the Free Port of [City]

### I. Constitutional Premises

The city is granted **conditional autonomy** under an Organic Law issued by the central government. The autonomy is **plenary on commercial matters**, **bounded on civic matters**, and **reserved to the center on sovereignty matters**. The six offices established below are interdependent — each office is both empowered and constrained by the others. The framework's central design principle: **flexibility is granted locally; legitimacy is anchored centrally; the courts are the referees when the balance breaks.**

---

### II. The Six Offices

#### 1. Ekklesia (Citizen Assembly) — the legitimacy floor

The ekklesia does not govern; it confers legitimacy. It uses a **three-tier participation structure**:

- **Tier 1 — Exclusive Ekklesia decisions:** local market regulation, public works, city sanitation, building codes. Simple majority.
- **Tier 2 — Joint decisions (ekklesia proposes, center ratifies):** tariff rate adjustments within center-set bounds, local law codification, public-safety force sizing. Two-thirds ekklesia majority; center must respond within 30 days or be deemed to have acquiesced.
- **Tier 3 — Advisory only:** diplomatic appointments, treaties with rival powers, emergency authorizations. Ekklesia files a dissent report that accompanies the central decision but does not bind.

**Anti-capture controls:**
- Citizenship threshold: 5 years residence for full vote; 10 years for boule candidacy.
- Boule candidates screened by central security against a published blacklist (contractor ties, >5% holdings, or near-relatives in rival-power bureaucracies).
- One commercial guild may hold at most one-third of boule seats.
- Minority-protection rule: any measure affecting a minority commercial community (>15% of the ekklesia) requires a separate majority among that community.
- A **Lustrator** (anonymous central auditor) reviews annually for vote-correlated capture (r > 0.7 triggers special inquiry).
- Every five years, a **Philepsia** (trust review) allows a 3/5 ekklesia majority to lodge a no-confidence motion against the archon; center must decide within 60 days.

#### 2. Boule (Merchant Council) — the engine of commercial flexibility

Twelve members elected from the security-vetted candidate list, **two consecutive one-year terms maximum**, staggered turnover so no more than half rotate at once.

**Tariff procedure (the core economic flex):**
- A Tariff Committee of ≥5 boule members drafts a schedule; published 10 days for objection; then boule votes.
- **Routine tariffs** (≤15% adjustment, <20 commodity lines): boule vote alone; reported to archon within 5 days.
- **Significant reforms** (>15%, new categories): boule proposes, archon ratifies within 30 days; if archon withholds, ekklesia may override by simple majority.
- **Emergency tariffs** (disruption, embargo, currency shock): 2/3 boule vote, reported to archon within 72 hours, expire in 60 days without standard ratification.
- **Diplomatic trade arrangements**: boule advises; archon negotiates; center approves; ekklesia informed.

**Legal adaptation:** boule may amend commercial law only by citing existing merchant custom or precedent, must not contradict central code, and **must include archon compatibility certification**. All adaptations expire after 5 years without renewal — preventing jurisdictional drift toward either rival power's law.

#### 3. Archon (Central Appointee) — the sovereignty anchor

Appointed by the center from a panel of three outsiders; boule selects one. **Three-year, non-renewable term; ten-year bar on reappointment.** No property, marriage, or litigation interest in the city or rival powers for the previous five years.

**Veto scope (the explicit list):**
1. Treaties and compacts with foreign powers (even informal ones).
2. Tariff schedules exceeding the center-set flex band.
3. Extraterritorial legal privileges for foreign merchants or envoys.
4. Admission of foreign consuls and accreditation of rhetores.
5. Decisions affecting the garrison, fortress access, or fortifications.
6. Constitutional amendments and Organic Law revisions.

**The archon has NO veto** (only a declaratory formal protest) over: internal tax assessment and land registration; cultural and religious ordinances.

**Foreign-facing credentials:** the archon issues joint credentials with the boule for any official who speaks for the city to foreign powers. License ≤12 months, names specific envoys/powers, lists express limitations. Revocation is unilateral by archon; center may override within 60 days. A **credential ledger** is sealed monthly with the center and the city recorder.

**Court relationship:** the archon does not sit as judge. Prosecutes only **two categories** — treason and foreign corruption (accepting payment, gift, or direction from a foreign power). Manufacturing a foreign-corruption charge against a political opponent is itself a removable offense.

#### 4. Strategos (Garrison Commander) — the security veto

Appointed by the center. Confirmed by boule and archon, but a 60-day consultation period ends with center appointment standing unless both houses formally declare conflict of interest and the center concurs. **Dual reporting:** provincial archon (routine) and theater commander (intelligence and contingency), via two independent courier routes.

**24-month rotation** with 30-day overlap (predecessor present as observer). Prohibited from holding property in the city, marrying a resident, or private trade. Quarterly financial disclosure to the dikasterion.

**Asset allocation:**
- **Central control** (non-negotiable): city walls and gates, customs forts on the approaches, intelligence bureau, artillery/siege arms.
- **Local control**: city watch (limited to spears and short swords), market police, neighborhood defense corps (sidearms only).
- Annual weapons inventory by the strategos.

**Override powers (the most dangerous instrument, tightly bounded):**
- Triggered only by: confirmed foreign intelligence operation, imminent external threat, or credible coup evidence.
- Must file a **proclamation of necessity** with the provincial archon and theater commander simultaneously, and post publicly in the agora within 6 hours.
- May seal gates (max 72 hours), detain named individuals (max 48 hours), requisition goods with archon-set compensation within 30 days.
- **MAY NOT** override to collect taxes, arrest for speech/commerce, install/remove officials, or modify commercial agreements.
- Boule may petition the dikasterion to vacate within 15 days; any override exceeding 72 hours requires theater-commander approval.

**Counter-intelligence posture:** a three-tier system (green/yellow/red) refreshed monthly. A **merchant-contact register** requires any contact between a foreign diplomatic agent and a city merchant beyond routine customs brokerage to be reported within 24 hours. Failure to report is a commercial-code violation (fine, suspension), not a security crime. The bureau does not surveil ordinary commerce.

#### 5. Rhetor (Diplomatic Spokesperson) — the controlled foreign voice

Appointed on conjoint archon–boule credentials, license ≤12 months. Holds a **Segmented Credential Letter** that explicitly partitions authority:

**Requires pre-clearance from the archon (≥72 hours):**
1. Tariff or trade-preference commitments outlasting the session.
2. Legal/judicial reciprocity agreements.
3. Diplomatic recognition or protocol.
4. Concessions affecting central revenue.
5. Security or military arrangements.

**Full discretion on the spot:**
1. Procedural arrangements (schedules, venues, interpreters).
2. Preliminary commercial offers and counter-offers.
3. Non-binding goodwill language.
4. Requests for clarification.
5. Hospitality and cultural exchange logistics.

**Reporting regime:**
- **4-hour flash report** to archon and boule secretary.
- **48-hour full procès-verbal** filed with the dikasterion clerk — **publicly accessible and immutable**.
- **Monthly digest** to the boule.
- **On-demand audit** by the dikasterion; failure to appear = immediate revocation.

**Political-defense script (rehearsed, not improvised):** When the rival-power negotiator attempts to convert a commercial exchange into a political-alignment conversation, the rhetor deploys one of three scripted moves — *The Fidelity Pivot, The Mandate Boundary, The Counter-Offer Redirect* — none of which improvises political disclaimers.

**Sunset:** any commitment outside the credential letter is **void ab initio**; the foreign party bears the risk. **No retroactive ratification** by the rhetor (only the archon may re-issue credentials, requiring a fresh cycle). Revocation triggers a 72-hour boule replacement, **Euthynai audit** within 30 days, certified notification to foreign powers.

#### 6. Dikasterion (Local Court) — the referee

The court's first-instance arm is the **symbouleutikon dikasterion** (commercial chamber), drawn by lot from the citizen body.

**Jurisdiction:**
- First instance: disputes between two residents, or any contract performed in city territory.
- Any case involving a foreign merchant requires a neutral arbitrator from a shared-trade roster or referral to the central commercial chamber.
- **Emergency injunction access** for foreign merchants is guaranteed by statute — they bypass the 30-day wait to reach the central court directly.

**Two-tier appeals:**
- First appeal to the central commercial bureau within 30 days.
- Second appeal only on manifest error of law or denial of due process to the full central tribunal.

**Veto reviewability** (the archon is not above the law):
- The boule has standing to petition the central dikasterion within 45 days.
- Three grounds for reversal: (1) ultra vires (the matter wasn't a sovereignty matter), (2) procedural default (no written reasoned decision within 15 days), (3) manifest error (stated grounds are pretextual).
- Reversed vetoes cannot be re-issued on the same resolution (contempt).

**Override due process (the rail around the strategos):**
- 48-hour sworn declaration to the central dikasterion; failure to file = void.
- 20-day window for any affected person to challenge; burden on the strategos.
- Property seized must be inventoried by a neutral magistrate; unjustified seizure is paid from the strategos's office, not the city.
- No override >60 days without renewal; detention >72 hours requires a judicial warrant.
- Citizens may not be expelled under override — only detained pending review.

**Diplomatic-act liability (the three-category rule):**
- **Within mandate** → bind the city as if the archon had acted.
- **Exceeds mandate but ratifiable** → provisional 90-day binding; silence = rejection; rhetor faces internal discipline but the city's provisional liability persists.
- **Ultra vires** → void; foreign party in good faith has a claim against the rhetor personally; city must disavow within 30 days or be deemed to have ratified by acquiescence.

**Mandatory review checklist (any major city decision must pass):**
1. Legal basis cited.
2. Non-discrimination audit.
3. Due process compliance.
4. Veto screen (with any judicial review).
5. Override clearance (48-hour filing and 20-day window).
6. Mandate verification for diplomatic acts.
7. Publication and notice to the central commercial bureau within 10 days.
8. Appeal forum and deadlines stated.

---

### III. How the Six Offices Interlock

The design is a **three-by-two matrix**:

|               | **Local** | **Central** |
|---|---|---|
| **Economic** | Boule (tariff/law) | Archon (veto + credentials) |
| **Legitimacy** | Ekklesia (three tiers) | Center (Organic Law + archon selection) |
| **Security** | Strategos (garrison) | Rhetor (foreign-facing) |
| **Judicial** | Dikasterion (first instance) | Central tribunal (final appeal) |

Every office has **both an empowerment and a check**. The boule can set tariffs but the archon can veto; the archon can veto but the dikasterion can reverse; the strategos can override but the dikasterion can vacate; the rhetor can speak but the archon accredits and revokes; the ekklesia confers legitimacy but cannot decide sovereignty; the dikasterion adjudicates but is itself drawn by lot and cannot be packed or prorogued.

---

### IV. Three Worked Examples

**Example 1 — Tariff adjustment (the flex in action):**
A merchant guild petitions the boule to raise third-country spice tariffs from 12% to 18%. Boule forms a 3-member tariff review group; members with spice holdings recuse. Ekklesia deliberates for 2 hours; quorum 40% of registered citizens met; a 15% compromise passes by simple majority. Boule reports to archon within 5 days; archon ratifies within 30 days (within flex band, no veto triggered). New rate takes effect on the first day of next market month. Boule reports revenue quarterly; if revenues drop >8% for two consecutive quarters, ekklesia can reopen.

**Example 2 — Rival-power co-option attempt (the rules trip the trap):**
A rival-power negotiator meets the rhetor and proposes, "Your city clearly has interests distinct from the capital; let us discuss your independent future." The rhetor deploys **The Mandate Boundary**: *"I note you speak of interests beyond my charge. I shall convey your words to the archon. But I cannot receive proposals outside my credentials, nor commit the city to any position not pre-cleared."* The 4-hour flash report files the incident. The strategos's merchant-contact register flags the meeting within 24 hours. The dikasterion retains the 48-hour procès-verbal as evidence. The boule's Lustrator reviews the next quarter for correlated voting anomalies. The rival power gains no opening.

**Example 3 — Archon overreach (the veto gets reversed):**
The boule passes a resolution easing internal land-registration fees. The archon vetoes on "sovereignty" grounds. The boule petitions the central dikasterion within 45 days on the ground that internal land registration is on the archon's **non-veto list** — the archon may lodge a formal protest but not block. The central dikasterion reverses the veto as ultra vires; the original resolution takes effect. The archon may not re-issue the veto on the same resolution.

---

### V. Sunset and Amendment

The Organic Law is reviewed every ten years. Any amendment requires: a two-thirds boule vote, a simple-majority ekklesia vote, and center ratification. No amendment may extinguish the ekklesia's three-tier rights, the archon's term limits, the strategos's no-tax-no-speech override constraints, the rhetor's void-ab-initio rule, or the dikasterion's veto-reviewability. These are the **unalterable core** of the city's autonomy.

— End of Framework —

**Political-defense script (rehearsed, not improvised):** When the rival-power negotiator attempts to convert a commercial exchange into a political-alignment conversation, the rhetor deploys one of three scripted moves — *The Fidelity Pivot, The Mandate Boundary, The Counter-Offer Redirect* — none of which improvises political disclaimers.

**Sunset:** any commitment outside the credential letter is **void ab initio**; the foreign party bears the risk. **No retroactive ratification** by the rhetor (only the archon may re-issue credentials, requiring a fresh cycle). Revocation triggers a 72-hour boule replacement, **Euthynai audit** within 30 days, certified notification to foreign powers.

#### 6. Dikasterion (Local Court) — the referee

The court's first-instance arm is the **symbouleutikon dikasterion** (commercial chamber), drawn by lot from the citizen body.

**Jurisdiction:**
- First instance: disputes between two residents, or any contract performed in city territory.
- Any case involving a foreign merchant requires a neutral arbitrator from a shared-trade roster or referral to the central commercial chamber.
- **Emergency injunction access** for foreign merchants is guaranteed by statute — they bypass the 30-day wait to reach the central court directly.

**Two-tier appeals:**
- First appeal to the central commercial bureau within 30 days.
- Second appeal only on manifest error of law or denial of due process to the full central tribunal.

**Veto reviewability** (the archon is not above the law):
- The boule has standing to petition the central dikasterion within 45 days.
- Three grounds for reversal: (1) ultra vires (the matter wasn't a sovereignty matter), (2) procedural default (no written reasoned decision within 15 days), (3) manifest error (stated grounds are pretextual).
- Reversed vetoes cannot be re-issued on the same resolution (contempt).

**Override due process (the rail around the strategos):**
- 48-hour sworn declaration to the central dikasterion; failure to file = void.
- 20-day window for any affected person to challenge; burden on the strategos.
- Property seized must be inventoried by a neutral magistrate; unjustified seizure is paid from the strategos's office, not the city.
- No override >60 days without renewal; detention >72 hours requires a judicial warrant.
- Citizens may not be expelled under override — only detained pending review.

**Diplomatic-act liability (the three-category rule):**
- **Within mandate** → bind the city as if the archon had acted.
- **Exceeds mandate but ratifiable** → provisional 90-day binding; silence = rejection; rhetor faces internal discipline but the city's provisional liability persists.
- **Ultra vires** → void; foreign party in good faith has a claim against the rhetor personally; city must disavow within 30 days or be deemed to have ratified by acquiescence.

**Mandatory review checklist (any major city decision must pass):**
1. Legal basis cited.
2. Non-discrimination audit.
3. Due process compliance.
4. Veto screen (with any judicial review).
5. Override clearance (48-hour filing and 20-day window).
6. Mandate verification for diplomatic acts.
7. Publication and notice to the central commercial bureau within 10 days.
8. Appeal forum and deadlines stated.

---

### III. How the Six Offices Interlock

The design is a **three-by-two matrix**:

|               | **Local** | **Central** |
|---|---|---|
| **Economic** | Boule (tariff/law) | Archon (veto + credentials) |
| **Legitimacy** | Ekklesia (three tiers) | Center (Organic Law + archon selection) |
| **Security** | Strategos (garrison) | Rhetor (foreign-facing) |
| **Judicial** | Dikasterion (first instance) | Central tribunal (final appeal) |

Every office has **both an empowerment and a check**. The boule can set tariffs but the archon can veto; the archon can veto but the dikasterion can reverse; the strategos can override but the dikasterion can vacate; the rhetor can speak but the archon accredits and revokes; the ekklesia confers legitimacy but cannot decide sovereignty; the dikasterion adjudicates but is itself drawn by lot and cannot be packed or prorogued.

---

### IV. Three Worked Examples

**Example 1 — Tariff adjustment (the flex in action):**
A merchant guild petitions the boule to raise third-country spice tariffs from 12% to 18%. Boule forms a 3-member tariff review group; members with spice holdings recuse. Ekklesia deliberates for 2 hours; quorum 40% of registered citizens met; a 15% compromise passes by simple majority. Boule reports to archon within 5 days; archon ratifies within 30 days (within flex band, no veto triggered). New rate takes effect on the first day of next market month. Boule reports revenue quarterly; if revenues drop >8% for two consecutive quarters, ekklesia can reopen.

**Example 2 — Rival-power co-option attempt (the rules trip the trap):**
A rival-power negotiator meets the rhetor and proposes, "Your city clearly has interests distinct from the capital; let us discuss your independent future." The rhetor deploys **The Mandate Boundary**: *"I note you speak of interests beyond my charge. I shall convey your words to the archon. But I cannot receive proposals outside my credentials, nor commit the city to any position not pre-cleared."* The 4-hour flash report files the incident. The strategos's merchant-contact register flags the meeting within 24 hours. The dikasterion retains the 48-hour procès-verbal as evidence. The boule's Lustrator reviews the next quarter for correlated voting anomalies. The rival power gains no opening.

**Example 3 — Archon overreach (the veto gets reversed):**
The boule passes a resolution easing internal land-registration fees. The archon vetoes on "sovereignty" grounds. The boule petitions the central dikasterion within 45 days on the ground that internal land registration is on the archon's **non-veto list** — the archon may lodge a formal protest but not block. The central dikasterion reverses the veto as ultra vires; the original resolution takes effect. The archon may not re-issue the veto on the same resolution.

---

### V. Sunset and Amendment

The Organic Law is reviewed every ten years. Any amendment requires: a two-thirds boule vote, a simple-majority ekklesia vote, and center ratification. No amendment may extinguish the ekklesia's three-tier rights, the archon's term limits, the strategos's no-tax-no-speech override constraints, the rhetor's void-ab-initio rule, or the dikasterion's veto-reviewability. These are the **unalterable core** of the city's autonomy.

— End of Framework —
